sections.title: Every Level of a Claude Second Brain Explained

items.q: What should you remember about **Five levels, five questions**?
items.a: **(1) exact word/file lookup, (2) aggregate everything** on a topic, (3) semantic/meaning search, (4) trace relationship chains across entities, (5) always-on autonomous sync.

items.q: What should you remember about **Start at Level 1 always**?
items.a: **CLAUDE.md (or AGENTS.md) as router**: role + "where things live" rules; folders for context, projects, decisions.

items.q: What should you remember about **No proven standard folder layout**?
items.a: **routing clarity matters more than copying Nate's structure.**

items.q: What should you remember about **Level 2 adds wiki + memory**?
items.a: **Karpathy LLM Wiki for compounding knowledge;** Claude Code auto-memory writes memory.md; duplicate router as agents.md for Codex portability.

items.q: What should you remember about **Obsidian is optional**?
items.a: **visualization layer only; Nate** rarely opens it because agents read the same markdown.

items.q: What should you remember about **Vector search ≠ full context**?
items.a: **chunking breaks "summarize March 5 meeting" and "which** week had highest sales?"; use markdown for whole-document tasks, vectors for needle-in-haystack (e.g. "what was rule 17?").

items.q: What should you remember about **Mixed levels per folder**?
items.a: **one subfolder can be** Level 2 wiki while another is Level 3 vector index.

items.q: What should you remember about **Knowledge graphs need rich input**?
items.a: **use "Grill Me" skill (from Matt** Pocock) to interview yourself into brainstorm files before graph extraction pays off.

items.q: What should you remember about **Privacy tradeoff**?
items.a: **sending client/business data to** Anthropic via Claude Code; local/open-source alternatives exist for sensitive data.

items.q: What should you remember about **Evergreen vs transient**?
items.a: **ingest what you'll still want in a** year; route agents to ClickUp/Slack for live threads instead of copying noise into the vault.

items.q: What should you remember about **Lookup waterfall**?
items.a: **OTA file → wiki/meeting** transcripts → live ClickUp pull, in that order.

items.q: What should you remember about **Team second brains**?
items.a: **adoption and change management** harder than picking Drive vs Notion vs GitHub.
